title: Bechet and Benny Goodman battle at the Saratoga
summary: After Bechet returned from Europe Goodman challenged him on clarinet in a friendly battle; Holmes played Jimmy Dorsey's 'Sensation' solo and still preferred Hodges.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: And then one night, Benny Goodman came in with his clarinet. And Sidney Bechet had just come back from Europe, and naturally, Sidney, being from down in New Orleans, they were featuring him. Russell just announced him, and this-that-and-the-other. And Bechet was up there blowin'... And I was gettin' a big kick out of Bechet. You know, he was... At the time, his hair was white, he looked like older than what he really was. And he was blowin' the soprano. He was creating a lot of attention.

So Benny Goodman runs up on the stand and takes out his clarinet. He wants to know... He asked somebody, 'Who's that old man playing the soprano saxophone?' Benny takes his clarinet and they start to battling one another. And

that's all Sidney wanted to hear. And they just battled backward and forward, backward and forward, backward and forward. That was a great night in the Saratoga Club, because all the musicians were around and just the two of them, backwards and forwards.

It did me good because I didn't have to play it! Because Jimmy Dorsey was sitting up on the bandstand, you know, and I had just gotten up. Jimmy and I had just... Because at that time, Jimmy had recorded a number, a saxophone solo on a number "Sensation," and I knew the number -- I knew the solo, you know. And we was on the stand playing "Sensation," and just before Jimmy's solo, I played -- and I played his solo on the number. Which was very unprofessional, you know. And Jimmy was so surprised, he turned around and shook my hand!

Well, we had a good time, though. But right after that, then Bechet was introduced, and that's when him and Benny Goodman got to battlin' up there. But it was all in fun. Nobody got killed or anything in that battle.
No, no.
Yes, it was... Both of them were battlin', though. They was wailin', too.
Did Bechet play his clarinet as well as...
No, no, he played soprano.
Just the soprano, yeah.

He just played soprano, and then he played clarinet. But at that time, Benny... Benny was a good clarinet player. But he wasn't no... He's not like he is now, you know. Benny wasn't always great. He had to start, too. Yeah, he wasn't that great. He was good, but he wasn't always so great.
But of course, Sidney was a mature musician at that time.
Well, Sidney was...
A genius.

...an experienced musician. Benny was young. You know what I mean? Benny was a youngster. Sidney, he had been to Europe and back and one thing or another, and he had a lot of experience. Good musician. He had his ideas. He really had ideas, too. Yeah, good man.
You were probably as impressed with Bechet as Johnny Hodges was.
Not quite the same way.
Not quite the same way.

Sidney did not impress me... I mean, he was a good saxophone player, and I was thrilled when I heard him. You know, naturally I would be thrilled. But to me, see, I was always Johnny Hodges. He didn't sound as good to

me as Johnny Hodges did. He never did -- to me. But I mean, that's the way I thought about it. That's my own personal opinion. Now, Johnny, he was wrapped up in Bechet. And I don't know why, because to me Johnny sounded immediate(?) to me. But that's an opinion. That's just... Well, that's what makes (?). Well, he was pretty good, I think.
That's an exciting evening at the Saratoga Club.
Oh yeah.
About what year do you think that must have been?
Oh, it's hard for me to say. I don't know. It could have been in... In the Thirties maybe. In the Thirties. The early Thirties.
Well, now, you wrote some numbers yourself which were recorded.
Yeah, yeah. We don't normally write any of my music. I might leave a symphony or something out there, you know. After all, I did play with a symphony band, you know. I started at the top.
[PAUSE]
